name: Replace A Dead Sora Video Step With Kie.ai

parameters.content:
## Replace A Dead Sora Video Step With Kie.ai

The Sora 2 API was switched off on 24 September 2026 and no official
replacement was offered, so every workflow with a Sora step in it now errors.
This is a drop-in sub-workflow to put in that gap: delete the broken node, add
an Execute Sub-workflow node pointing here, pass a prompt, get a video back.

### How it works

The caller sends a prompt and, optionally, duration, aspect ratio, resolution
and a first frame. Those are normalised and clamped, then hashed into a job
key, and an identical job already in the ledger returns its stored video
without paying for a second render. New jobs run down a model chain. Each
provider on Kie.ai names its input fields differently, so the neutral job is
translated per model before it is submitted. Rendering is asynchronous, so the
workflow polls every twenty seconds and gives up on a model after five minutes
rather than hanging, and a model that fails, times out or turns out not to
exist hands over to the next one. That chain is the real lesson of the
shutdown: a single hard-coded provider is one deprecation from a dead
workflow. The winning video is downloaded, saved to Drive and written to the
ledger with the credits every attempt consumed, so cost is visible rather than
a surprise. The caller always gets one flat answer with the trail of what was
tried.

### Setup

Add your Kie.ai key as a header credential, connect Drive, set the folder, and
create the data table with the columns named on the cache node.

### Customization

Reorder or extend the model chain, change the poll interval and ceiling, or
drop the Drive step and keep the hosted URL.

## Take the job, and do not pay twice
The caller's prompt is normalised and clamped, then hashed into a job key. An identical job already in the ledger returns its stored video instead of rendering again.

## Try each model until one delivers
Each provider's input fields differ, so the job is translated per model. Rendering is asynchronous, so this polls every twenty seconds and gives up after five minutes, then moves to the next model.

## Hand back one flat answer
The winning video is downloaded, stored in Drive and written to the ledger with the credits every attempt consumed. A total failure returns the reason rather than nothing.

## Optional: run it on its own
This pair lets you test the sub-workflow from the editor without a calling workflow. Delete both once your own workflow is wired in.

assignments.name: prompt
assignments.value: A slow push-in on a ceramic coffee cup on a wooden counter, morning light, steam rising

nodes.name: Called By Your Workflow
nodes.notes: Point your old Sora step at this workflow with an Execute Sub-workflow node. Pass prompt, and optionally durationSeconds, aspectRatio, resolution, firstFrameUrl, callbackUrl and modelChain.

nodes.name: Look Up Render Cache
nodes.notes: Data table columns: jobKey (string), videoUrl (string), driveFileId (string), model (string), creditsConsumed (number), renderedAtMs (number)

nodes.name: Wait Before Polling
nodes.notes: Twenty seconds between polls. Never leave this node empty: an empty Wait defaults to one hour.

nodes.name: Render Settled Or Out Of Time?
nodes.notes: Fifteen polls at twenty seconds is a five minute ceiling per model, after which this model is treated as failed and the chain moves on.

main.node: Render Settled Or Out Of Time?
